title: Quasi-contract, quantum meruit, and restitution
summary: The historical action names overlap with, but do not exhaust, the broader subject of restitution.
notes: Quasi-contract refers to recovery at common law without a true contractual undertaking. Quantum meruit historically concerns the worth of services; quantum valebant concerns the worth of goods. The book notes imprecise interchangeable usage. Use the underlying basis—promise, actual agreement, or unjust enrichment—to clarify a claim instead of treating the label alone as an element test.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 145–146. Open assigned page 145.
